thread:
maria: Quick summary from the Lyra-lite-9b bring-up. Ran fp16 / int8 / int4 across our short-chat and longform summarization slices. Int4 gives ~2.3x token-cost reduction vs fp16, latency unchanged for short requests, but we see a quality drop on longform (>1024 tokens) slices. Details below.

aleks: Can you drop the numbers? what metrics did you use for "quality drop"?
maria: Sure — aggregated over our QA+Summarize suite (1k eval examples): short-chat (avg input < 256): int4 delta vs fp16 = -0.2% EM, -0.4 BLEU (within noise). longform summarization (avg output ~1.5k tokens): ROUGE-L: fp16 42.1 -> int8 41.6 -> int4 38.8 (int4 = -3.3 pts vs fp16). human preference A/B for longform: 64% prefer fp16 vs int4.
shayna: That ROUGE drop is pretty material for product longform customers. What's the token-econ?
maria: Token cost assumptions from our pricing: fp16 unit cost = $X per 1M tokens (baseline), int8 = ~0.6x, int4 = ~0.43x. So int4 reduces model compute spend by ~57% vs fp16. For a typical longform request (2k generated tokens) cost goes from 0.002X -> 0.00086X saved ~0.00114X per request. But quality loss might increase downstream support tickets / regression risk.
nico: Do we have latency / tail numbers and batch behavior?
maria: P50 p95 p99 short-chat (batching off for latency): fp16 45ms/120ms/220ms, int8 48/130/240, int4 44/125/230. For longform (streaming token generation): throughput (tokens/sec) fp16 320, int8 360, int4 420. So int4 improves throughput and per-token latency; tail behavior roughly similar, slight jitter on p99 for int4 with longcontext when KV cache growth > 1M entries.
aleks: Anything in the logs re: numeric instabilities or bad tokens?
maria: We saw isolated cases (~0.6% of evals) where int4 emitted repeated tokens on the end of generation in summarization tasks. Repro steps attached.
ops-bot: CI smoke run completed — all infra checks passed for int4 container.
shayna: Product asks: what do we recommend for GTN (general traffic routing)? Options: full switch, hybrid routing by length, or keep int8 only.
maria: My recommendation: hybrid routing + canary. Concrete proposal: default route short requests (<512 input tokens or expected output <512) -> int4, otherwise route to int8. Canary: start with 3% traffic to int4 for longform, 20% for short-chat. Monitor metrics: ROUGE-L / human-pref / regeneration-rate / defect tickets. SLO: no more than 1.5 pt ROUGE-L degradation on longform over 7 days and no >2x increase in regeneration rate.
nico: Sounds reasonable. How to implement flagging in routing config?
maria: Example routing rule (pseudocode):
```
route:
  - match: input_tokens < 512
    model: lyra-lite-9b-int4
    percent: 80
  - match: input_tokens >= 512
    model: lyra-lite-9b-int8
    percent: 95
  - fallback: lyra-lite-9b-fp16
    percent: 5
```
We want a small fallback to fp16 for high-value customers or when int8 capacity constrained.
aleks: For canary metrics, can we compute expected sample size? If longform traffic is low, 3% may not surface regressions fast.
maria: Agreed — if daily longform volume < 5k requests, increase longform canary to 10% until we gather 10k longform samples. Use prioritized sampling on high-variance prompts.
shayna: For GTN messaging: recommend this to teams as "cost-safety hybrid" with conservative thresholds and an ops escalation path. Also include a suggested rollout calendar: week 0 canary, week 1 ramp to 25% for short-chat, week 2 evaluate and decide on longform ramp.
nico: Any changes needed on the eval harness? We should add targeted longform regression tests and a recall-check slice.
maria: Yes adding these: (1) expanded longform human A/B panel (500 ex), (2) automated detect for repetition/hallucination spikes, (3) token-level KL and prefix recall. I'll open an eval PR.
shayna: One more ask — cost modelling for sales/GTN: provide per-customer savings estimate and break-even threshold given quality adjustments. Can you draft a quick template?
maria: I'll mock one with two scenarios: conservative (assume 2 pt ROUGE penalty costed at $Y per ticket) and optimistic (no downstream cost). Template fields: baseline qps, avg tokens/request, int4 unit cost multiplier, expected ROUGE delta, expected ticket rate multiplier.
aleks: OK. Next steps: maria to open PR with routing + eval changes, create a canary run and share dashboard. shayna to draft GTN note and recommended customer messaging. nico to scope infra capacity for int4 pools. ops-bot: slack alert channel created #canary-lyra-lite-int4.
maria: Filing the PR now — will ping when dashboard is live. :eyes:
